summary.text: PA12-GF is glass-fibre-filled polyamide 12. A maker sells it for functional parts and for parts that absorb kinetic energy or repeated shock, and a maker stresses its very low moisture absorption. Its HDT at 0.45 MPa is 150 °C. On the H2C it prints at 255⁠–⁠270 °C and needs a hardened nozzle, and a sheet asks for more chamber heat than the H2C reaches.

items.agent: Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature
items.text: Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis... polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

items.agent: Hot water or moist air at higher temperatures
items.text: Polycondensation products, to which polyamides also belong, have a limited resistance to hot water or moist air at higher temperatures. PA 12 has good hydrolysis resistance compared to other polyamides, but it is gradually molecularly degraded by hot water. Compounds with a high molecular mass will last longer than those with a low molecular mass. Hydrolytic degradation occurs faster in acid media than in neutral or alkaline media. Standard compounds are resistant to pure water to about 70 or 80 °C.

Exposure to short wave light of wavelengths less than 400 nm results in an accelerated decrease in the molecular mass of the polymers, causing molded parts and semi-finished products to become brittle. Light stabilizers, UV absorbers and/or radical scavengers considerably reduce weathering damage. However, the best protection is provided by suitable grades of carbon black, if blackening is possible.
Most VESTAMID compounds are flammable. At mass temperatures above 350 °C flammable gases form through decomposition.
items.note: No UL 94 rating for the neat resin is stated. Verdict convention used in this table: burns / UL 94 HB = not-resistant, V-1 or V-2 = limited, V-0 = resistant.
